blueprint.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

item.vignette: A 15-year-old boy is evaluated for progressive gait instability. Examination shows dysarthria, loss of vibration and position sense in the lower extremities, absent ankle reflexes, and extensor plantar responses. He has pes cavus and scoliosis. Echocardiography shows concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Genetic testing demonstrates biallelic expansion of a GAA trinucleotide repeat in the FXN gene.
item.lead_in: Which of the following molecular consequences most directly causes this disorder?

options.A: Production of an abnormally elongated polyglutamine-containing huntingtin protein
options.B: Silencing of FMR1 after expansion of a CGG repeat
options.C: Reduced production of frataxin, impairing normal mitochondrial function
options.D: Loss of the active maternal UBE3A allele in neurons
options.E: Reduced MECP2-dependent regulation of neuronal gene expression

explanation.key_explanation: Friedreich ataxia is usually caused by biallelic GAA-repeat expansion in FXN. The expansion markedly reduces frataxin production. Frataxin is required for normal mitochondrial function, and deficiency preferentially injures neurologic and cardiac tissues.

distractor_explanations.A: An expanded CAG repeat in HTT produces an elongated huntingtin protein in Huntington disease, not the biallelic FXN-associated phenotype.
distractor_explanations.B: A full FMR1 CGG expansion silences FMR1 in fragile X syndrome, which does not produce this sensory ataxia-cardiomyopathy pattern.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. The FXN GAA expansion reduces frataxin expression and disrupts mitochondrial function.
distractor_explanations.D: Loss of maternal UBE3A activity in neurons causes Angelman syndrome.
distractor_explanations.E: MECP2 loss of function causes Rett syndrome, typically with developmental regression in girls.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect biallelic FXN GAA-repeat expansion with reduced frataxin production and mitochondrial dysfunction in Friedreich ataxia.

evidence_map.claim: HTT CAG expansion causes an abnormally elongated huntingtin protein and is a different trinucleotide-repeat disorder.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not match the biallelic FXN GAA expansion in the stem.

evidence_map.claim: FMR1 CGG expansion above 200 silences FMR1 and causes fragile X syndrome.
FXN GAA-repeat expansion reduces frataxin production and disrupts normal mitochondrial function.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Explains the neurologic and cardiac findings.

evidence_map.claim: Loss of maternal UBE3A function in CNS neurons causes Angelman syndrome.
MECP2 variants alter neuronal gene regulation and cause Rett syndrome.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not fit the patient's genotype or phenotype.

sources.title: Friedreich ataxia: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: FXN GAA repeat expansion reduces frataxin production; frataxin is important for normal mitochondrial function.

sources.title: HTT gene: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: HTT CAG expansion produces an abnormally long huntingtin protein with toxic neuronal effects and anticipation.

sources.title: Fragile X syndrome: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: An FMR1 CGG repeat expansion above 200 silences FMR1 and prevents normal FMRP production.

sources.title: Angelman syndrome: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: In CNS neurons, the maternal UBE3A copy is active; loss of maternal UBE3A function causes Angelman syndrome.

sources.title: Rett syndrome: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: Classic Rett syndrome is usually caused by MECP2 variants; MeCP2 participates in regulation of gene activity and normal neuronal function.
